en: Oṃ, salutation to Śiva. Then the twilight [ritual] (saṃdhyā). Nośiya. Oṃ hrāṃ, svāhā to the principle of the self (ātmatattva). Oṃ hrīṃ, svāhā to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva). Oṃ hrūṃ, svāhā to the principle of Śiva (śivatattva).
Aiṃ: on the two nostrils (2), on the two ears (2), heart, head, and crest. Oṃ: the mutual union. (3)

*Hnasahnāsathīya* || *Nyāsa* || Salutations to you in the form of Rudra; *hraḥ*, for the great *pāśupata* weapon, *phaṭ*. Oṃ *hrāṃ* Aghora *hrāṃ*, salutations to the little finger (*kaniṣṭhikā*). Oṃ *hrāṃ* Thaghora *hrīṃ*, salutations to the ring finger (*anāmikā*). Oṃ *hrāṃ* Ghoraghorantare *hūṃ*.

Homage to Madhyamā. Oṃ hrāṃ sarvata sarva sarve hraiṃ; homage to Tarjanī. Oṃ hrāṃ jūṃ saḥ; homage to Aṅguṣṭha, whose nature is the form of light, hrauṃ. Homage to you in the form of Rudra, hraḥ, the Great Pāśupata.

*Astrāya phaṭ* || *Oṃ hrāṃ aghore hrāṃ sarvajñātā hṛdayāya namaḥ* || *Oṃ hrāṃ thaghore hrīṃ brahma śirase svāhā* || *Oṃ hrāṃ ghoraghoranta hūṃ jvālinī śikhāyai vauṣaṭ* || *Oṃ hrāṃ sarvata sarva sarve hrai kavacāya hūṃ* || *Oṃ hrāṃ juṃ saḥ* ||
Hrauṃ, vaṣaṭ to the three eyes, whose nature is the form of light. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to you who possess the form of Rudra;
hraḥ, phaṭ to the great Pāśupata weapon! Thus is the ritual placement (nyāsa) on the hands and limbs.

Oṃ hrāṃ kṣaṃ, obeisance to Īśāna, the upward-facing mouth. Oṃ hrāṃ yaṃ, obeisance to Tatpuruṣa, the eastern-facing mouth. Oṃ hrāṃ raṃ, obeisance to Aghora, the southern-facing mouth. Oṃ hrāṃ vaṃ, obeisance to Vāmadeva, the northern-facing mouth. Oṃ hrāṃ laṃ, [obeisance] to Sadyojāta...
Homage to the western face. *Oṃ hrāṃ kṣāṃ*, homage to Īśāna, the supreme upper face. Thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the faces.
For the purification of the food offering (*tāhāra-posala*): Oṃ, obeisance to Gaṅgā. Oṃ, obeisance to Yamunā.
Oṃ, obeisance to Narmadā. Oṃ, obeisance to Kāverī. Oṃ, obeisance to Sarasvatī. Oṃ, obeisance to Gaṇḍakī. Oṃ, obeisance to Kauśikī. Oṃ, obeisance to Godāvarī. [Recite] the mantra.

Oṃ japaṃ gṛhāṇa svāhā. [Touching] the head: Laṃ khataṃne. Oṃ hrāṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ. Oṃ hrīṃ śirase svāhā. Oṃ hrūṃ śikhāyai vauṣaṭ. Oṃ hreṃ kavacāya hūṃ. Oṃ hrūṃ netratrayāya vauṣaṭ. Prāṇāyāma. Oṃ hrāṃ, Rudra is the seer (ṛṣi), Agni is the deity, Gāyatrī is the meter.
The application of the *svacchanda* breath-control (*prāṇāyāma*): Oṃ hrāṃ, to the left nostril.
Oṃ hrīṃ, [meditate] upon the right nostril. Oṃ hrāṃ, having meditated upon the form of the deity:

yaṃ (10), raṃ (10), vaṃ (10). Then the meditation: Nośiya. Oṃ hrāṃ, [the mantra] beginning with "to the reality of the self" (*ātmatattvāya*), etc. The ritual placement (*nyāsa*): Oṃ hrīṃ, [to the one] whose excellent garland of ornaments is red, whose sacred thread is made of matted hair.
The young maiden has a swan as her seat,
four faces, and four arms.
Holding a sacrificial ladle and a rosary in her right hands, and a staff and a water-pot in her left,
she is the Brāhmaṇī at the three junctions of the day, when the excellent morning prayer has been performed.

Then the Gāyatrī: Oṃ hrāṃ, may we know that Great Lord; may we meditate upon Mahādeva; may Raudra inspire us. Recitation (10 times). Oṃ, for the purpose of destroying all sins and fulfilling desires, accept this recitation, svāhā! Oṃ hrāṃ, the auspiciousness of Āditya.
Knowledge [is] Śiva in the form of the Sun; there is no interval between the Sun and Śiva. Thus ends the midday *saṃdhyā*. *Nośiye*. *Nyāsa*: *Oṃ hrāṃ* to all the gods, *svāhā*.
*Oṃ hrāṃ* to all the mantras.

Svāhā! Oṃ hrāṃ, svāhā to all the ṛṣis! Oṃ hrāṃ, svāhā to all the Manus! Oṃ hrāṃ, svāhā to all human beings! Oṃ hrāṃ, svāhā to all the ancestors! Oṃ hrāṃ, svāhā to all the mothers! Oṃ hrāṃ, svāhā to all the bhūtas!

Svāhā! Oṃ hrāṃ, svāhā to all the piśācas! Oṃ hrāṃ, svāhā to all the chosen deities (iṣṭadevatās)! Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ, obeisance to Sūrya! Oṃ haṃ ṣaṃ, obeisance to the solar form (sūryamūrti) of Ṣoraka! Oṃ...
Salutations to the one accompanied by Prakāśaka and Tisā. Oṃ Hrīṃ Ccha, salutations to Nārāyaṇa, the soul of the universe.
Oṃ Hrīṃ, salutations to the one accompanied by Lakṣmī-Śakti. Oṃ Hrīṃ Aghore Hrīṃ Thaghore Hrīṃ Ghoraghorantare Hūṃ Phre Sarvataḥ.

Sarva sarve hre ju saḥ hrauṃ! Obeisance to Sadāśiva in the form of Rudra, to the Great Bhairava, the self-willed one (Svacchanda-bhaṭṭāraka). Oṃ hrīṃ! Obeisance to Aghoreśvarī together with her Śakti. Oṃ juṃ saḥ! [Obeisance] to Mṛtyuñjaya.

Salutation to Amṛteśvarī Mahābhairavī, to Netrabhaṭṭārikā, and to Sadāśivā. Oṃ juṃ saḥ, salutation to Amṛtalakṣmī together with Śakti. For the ritual placement (nyāsa): Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the Self residing in the heart; hraḥ, phaṭ, to the weapon-mantra. Thus concludes the procedure for the twilight rites (saṃdhyā-vidhi).
Next, the procedure for the worship of the *liṅga* is written down. Homage to the Guru.
He by whom the moving and unmoving world is pervaded, appearing as an unbroken, complete circle.
Salutation to that glorious Guru by whom that state has been revealed.
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is the god Maheśvara;
the Guru is indeed the entire universe—to that glorious Guru, I offer salutations.
The sandals of the venerable Śrī Parameṣṭhī Guru, the venerable Śrī Paramācārya, and the venerable Ādideva.
Sandals for the Lotus Seat. Sandals for the Argha-vessel Seat. Nyāsa: Oṃ Raṃ Astrāya Phaṭ. Aḥ Hṛdayāya Namaḥ. Akkāya Śirase Svāhā. Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ Jvālinī Śikhāyai Vauṣaṭ. Hūṃ Kavacāya.
HŪṂ | BHĀ | VAṢAṬ to the three eyes. RAṂ | PHAṬ to the weapon. Thus is the ritual assignment (nyāsa) of the hands and limbs.

*Oṃ aghapātrāsanāya namaḥ*. *A hṛdayāya namaḥ*, and so forth. [Perform] the invocation (*āvāhana*) and other rites. *Namaḥ* to the sandalwood, unbroken rice, and flowers. One should sprinkle [the water] upon oneself. *Namaḥ* to the sandalwood for the self-head (*ātma-śiras*). *Namaḥ* to the flower for the self-head. *Namaḥ* to the seat (*āsana*) of the self. *Namaḥ* to the form of the self (*ātma-mūrti*). *Oṃ*.
Salutation to the one seated on a tortoise. Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ, salutation to Sūrya. [Hands joined in] añjali.
(3) Oṃ heṣaṣoraka, salutation to the form of Sūrya. Oṃ, salutation to the one accompanied by Prakāśakti. Oṃ, we meditate upon the one with a thousand rays.

We meditate upon that for our success; may Sūrya impel us toward it. Invocation, installation, sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers—obeisance! Recitation: *Oṃ hrāṃ svāhā* (ten times). Assignment (*nyāsa*): *Oṃ chaṃ namo nārāyaṇāya astrāya phaṭ*. *Chaṃ namo nārāyaṇāya hṛdayāya namaḥ*. *Chaṃ*...
Namo nārāyaṇāya, to the head, svāhā! Chaṃ, namo nārāyaṇāya, to the crest-lock, vauṣaṭ!
Chaṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, for the armor: Hūṃ. Chaṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, for the three eyes:
Vauṣaṭ. Chaṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, for the weapon: Phaṭ. The ritual placement on the hands and limbs (karāṅganyāsa): Oṃ, obeisance to the one seated upon Garuḍa.
Oṃ hrīṃ chaṃ, salutation to Nārāyaṇa, the soul of the universe; hrīṃ, salutation! With palms joined in reverence. (3)

Food offering: *Namaḥ*. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Lakṣmī together with Śakti. Food offering: *Namaḥ*. Oṃ hrīṃ, we know Vaiṣṇavī; we meditate upon Nārāyaṇa; may He impel us toward that goal. *Tanno arya pracodayāt*. Food offering: *Namaḥ*.
The recitation beginning with the invocation: *hrīṃ svāhā* (ten times).

Nyāsa: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to you who have the form of Rudra, hraḥ, and so forth. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the one seated upon the bull. Oṃ hrāṃ aghore hrīṃ, thaghore hrīṃ, ghoraghorantare hrūṃ phreṃ, sarvataḥ sarva sarva hraṃ ju saḥ hro, obeisance to the one with the form of Rudra, hraṃḥ; [this is] the Śikhā.
Salutation to Svacchanda Mahābhairava, who is Sadāśiva. (Three *añjali*s)
Food offering: *namaḥ*. *Oṃ hrīṃ*, obeisance to Aghoreśvarī together with her Śakti. Food offering: *namaḥ*.
Oṃ, may we know Śikhānātha; may we meditate upon Svacchanda; may that Rudra inspire us. Ḥ.
The recitation beginning with the invocation: Hrāṃ Svāhā (ten times).

Nyāsa: Oṃ juṃ saḥ, to the weapon (astra) of infinite power, phaṭ! Purification of the hands: Oṃ juṃ saḥ, obeisance to the heart of the omniscient one! Oṃ juṃ saḥ, svāhā to the head that pervades space! Oṃ juṃ saḥ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock of primordial awakening!

Oṃ juṃ saḥ hūṃ, to the armor of one’s own mantra, hūṃ. Oṃ ju saḥ, to the three eyes of unimpaired power, vauṣaṭ. Oṃ ju saḥ, to the weapon of infinite power, phaṭ. Oṃ ju saḥ, obeisance to the one whose seat is the bull. Oṃ ju saḥ, to Mṛtyuñjaya, the Great Bhairava, the Lord of Immortality.

Salutation to the venerable Netra, who is Sadāśiva. Three *añjali*s. Salutation to the food offering (*naivedya*). Oṃ juṃ saḥ, salutation to Amṛtalakṣmī together with Śakti. The recitation for the invocation and other rites: Oṃ ju saḥ svāhā, 108 times.
The Maṇḍalavīya. Composed [by *Name*]. Oṃ, homage to the glorious deity Sūrya.
I bow to that Sun of Śiva, who, through his skillful policy, has bestowed the fortune of knowledge upon people blinded by the darkness of delusion;
he who lies upon the coils of the serpent-king Śeṣa at the edge of the ocean, which is his own bed amidst the waters of the netherworld.

May Viṣṇu, the Lord of the three worlds, who removes all sins and is praised by Brahmā and the hosts of gods and sages with the mantras of the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas— while the serpent-gem blazes at the tip of his hood and his own breath flows forth—
protect me.
Padmanābha.
Even by giving hundreds of millions of cows made of the gold of Mount Meru, [one does not attain such merit].
O Śivadaṇa, the fruit of that is equal to five crores of horses.
Pure and peaceful, supreme through the grace of Śiva, the omniscient Lord of Indra, joyful, the Blessed One who is the leader of the lords, the bestower of all desires,
or the word-born state that grants the boon of speech, the sovereign of the power of Vāmā and the others.
O Conqueror of Death, protect me—you who destroy the fear of leprosy and the sorrow of disease.
I am a sinner, born of evil deeds, evil-natured, and originating from evil;
save me, O lotus-eyed one, you who are the remover of all sins, Hara, the destroyer.
There is no other refuge; you alone are my refuge.
Therefore, protect, protect me at all times with your compassion, O Supreme Goddess!

To the glorious Sūrya, to Nārāyaṇa, to Aghora Mṛtyuñjaya; in this ritual procedure for the worship of the Eye of Śiva, may everything be fully complete for me through this praise. This is the Aghora-nyāsa for Nyāsalikā: Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the Heart. Salutation to the Self (Ātman). Oṃ hrāṃ, phaṭ, salutation to the Weapon (Astra). [This is] the dismissal (viśarjana).
Thus ends the ritual procedure for the worship of the *liṅga*.
Oṃ, homage to the illustrious Kubjikā; homage!
Aiṁ (5). Salutation to that venerable Guru who has revealed that state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which the moving and unmoving world is pervaded.
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is the divine Maheśvara;
the Guru is the entire universe—salutations to that illustrious Guru.
The sandals of the venerable Śrī Parameṣṭhi-guru, the venerable Śrī Paramācārya, the venerable Ādideva.
Sandals for the Lotus Seat; sandals for the Argha-vessel Seat; sandals for the Tortoise Seat; sandals for the Self Seat. Ai Kiṇi Vicce Koṅkaṇāya Hraḥ, Phaṭ for the Weapon.
The sandals. Purification of the hands with a flower: HŪṂ Vajrapañjare SVĀHĀ. [End].
Aiṃ (5) cala makule kulamacare hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
Then the ritual placement (*nyāsa*): *kiṇi (2) vicce koṃkaṇāye hraṃḥ astrāya phaṭ*.

The Purification of the Vessel (Kalaśodhana): Homage to the Blessed One, the Lady of the Heart-Lotus! Hrāṃ, homage to the sandals of Śrī Aṅguṣṭhā! Hsphreṃ, homage to the sandals of Kubjikā, the Lamp of the Kula, Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, [and] to the sandals of her index finger!
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hūṃ, to Varvarashikha Hūṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals of Madhyamā; Aiṃ Ghore Aghore Aghoramukhi Bahurūpāyai Hreṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals of Anāmikā.
Aiṃ (5) Chāṃ Chīṃ, the sandals for Mahantārikā, [to be placed] on the little finger.
Aiṃ (5) Kiṇi (2) Vicce Koṅkanāyai Hraṃḥ Astrāya Phaṭ. [This is] the Karanyāsa.
Homage to the Blessed One, to the one whose heart is a lotus, to Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, to the upward-facing one; [I offer] the sandals.
Hsphreṁ, to Kubjikā, the Island of the Kula; Hrāṁ, to the venerable Eastern Face, [I offer] the sandals.
Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ, [salutation] to Varvarashikhā; Hūṃ Śrīṃ, [salutation] to Dakṣiṇavaktrā; the sandals.
Aiṃ (5) Ghore Aghore Aghorāmukhi Bahurūpāyai Hreṃ Śrīṃ, [I offer] the sandals to the Northern Face.
Aiṃ (5) Chāṃ Chīṃ, [salutation] to Mahāntārikā; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, [salutation to] the Western Face, the sandals.
Kiṇi (2), Vicce Koṅkaṇāyai Hraṃḥ Śrīṃ, [I offer] the sandals to Parāmparavaktrā.
The ritual placement on the face (vaktranyāsa).
Aiṃ 5. Salutation to the Blessed One, the Lotus of the Heart; Hrāṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to the Heart.
Hsphreṃ, to Kubjikā, the lamp of the Kula, Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, svāhā to the head.
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hūṃ, to the tawny-haired crest, hūṃ śrīṃ, to the crest, vauṣaṭ!
Aiṃ (5) Ghore, Aghore, Aghorāmukhī, Bahurūpāyai; Hrai Śrīṃ, to the one who is armor, Hūṃ.
Aiṃ (5) Chāṃ Chīṃ, vauṣaṭ to Mahantārikā, Hrāṃ Śrīṃ, to the one possessing three eyes.
Kiṇi (2) Vicce Koṅkaṇāyai Hraṃḥ Astrāya Phaṭ. [This is the] Aṅganyāsa.
To the water-vessel and the seat, [offer] the sandals.
Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ, for the empowerment of the hero Ānandaśaktibhairava, śkṣmlvryūṃ,

the sandals to the venerable Śrījalapātrabhaṭṭārikā. Having worshipped with the six limbs, [one performs] invocation, installation, the offering of unhusked grain and flowers— namas— and displays the dhenumudrā.
Aiṃ! We know Kubjikā; we meditate upon the Lamp of the Kula; may that Kubjikā inspire us.
With that mantra, one should perform the sprinkling of oneself and all the ritual substances.

The sandals for the seat of the *argha* vessel: *hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hraḥ prasphura (2) ghora (2) taratanu (2) cata (2) pracata (2) kaha (2) vama (2) dama (2) ghātaya (2) vighātaya (2) vighni (2) hūṃ (3) phaṭ ko śrīkomārikā vicce*.

Pādukāṃ || ŚKṢMLVRYŪṂ ĪṂ Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda Śrīmahāvidyārājeśvarī HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ ŚRĪ(-) Arghapātrabhaṭṭārikāyai Pādukāṃ || Having worshipped with the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga), [perform] the invocation and so forth.
The *yonimudrā* is the tenth. Thus ends the worship of the *argha* vessel.

Then, having formed the tortoise-mudrā (*kacchapamudrā*), one performs the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*) by means of the five-syllabled mantra (*pañcapraṇava-mantra*) in both direct and reverse order.

By the fire of knowledge, she is Kuleśvarī in the south, and the leader of the assembly of families in the western direction.

O Mother, the primordial state is the Blessed One, whose essence is the nature of consciousness; through the abundance of knowledge and will, she manifests as Hari, Hara, Brahmā, and the goddesses.
